actions.new_text: In Psa 77:3 moan (H1993) stands one word before meditate, in the parallel clause: when the speaker remembers God he moans, and when he meditates his spirit faints.
actions.checked: Psa 77:3: When I remember God, I moan; when I meditate, my spirit faints
actions.reason: evidence validation (B5): it said remembering brings moaning and meditating brings fainting; the verse joins them by when, not by cause

observations.why: it said the god may be musing and not hearing; the verse does not say he does not hear

actions.new_text: In 1Ki 18:27 cry (H7121I) stands five words before musing, in Elijah's taunt: they are to cry aloud, and their god may be musing, or in one of the other states he names.
actions.checked: 1Ki 18:27: Cry aloud, for he is a god. Either he is musing, or he is relieving himself
actions.reason: evidence validation (B5): it said the god may be musing and not hearing; the verse does not say he does not hear
